builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
summary: SALTO replaces repeated forward/adjoint solves through a numerical PDE simulator for finite-amplitude source inversion with a single trained Koopman model whose lifted transpose propagates sensors backward in one solve and answers candidate events with an encoder pass and an inner product. The cost is an offline training stage plus three structural constraints (anchoring to the simulator's linearized propagator, centered observables, block-triangular propagator), which require access to the simulator's tangent linearization and observable training data. It can fail when events are far outside the training amplitude or location distribution, when no differentiable simulator or its linearization is available, and its accuracy guarantees hold only in the vanishing-amplitude limit rather than for arbitrary perturbations.
rationale: The method targets PDE inverse problems with an available simulator and its linearized propagator, a workload outside typical LLM/ML production practice, and the claimed gains are validated only on three nonlinear PDE benchmarks, so adoption is premature without a matching scientific-inference workload.
technique: Lifted Koopman adjoints for finite-amplitude source inversion

claims.statement: SALTO replaces repeated forward/adjoint solves through a numerical PDE simulator for finite-amplitude source inversion with a single trained Koopman model whose lifted transpose propagates sensors backward in one solve and answers candidate events with an encoder pass and an inner product. The cost is an offline training stage plus three structural constraints (anchoring to the simulator's linearized propagator, centered observables, block-triangular propagator), which require access to the simulator's tangent linearization and observable training data. It can fail when events are far outside the training amplitude or location distribution, when no differentiable simulator or its linearization is available, and its accuracy guarantees hold only in the vanishing-amplitude limit rather than for arbitrary perturbations.

Posterior sampling for two interacting sources on a reaction-diffusion system at one-twentieth of the solver's cost, with measurement prediction error of 2-8% versus 41-165% for the classical adjoint.
